newsitem.title: UK: Gerrard offers 53.7 mln stg for King&Shax.
newsitem.headline: Gerrard offers 53.7 mln stg for King&Shax.

text.p: Financial services provider and stockbroker Gerrard & National Plc has made a recommended offer for financial holding company King & Shaxson Holdings valuing it at 53.7 million stg.
The companies said in a joint statement that the merger would create a strong broking and specialist banking group with 10 billion stg of funds under management.

The offer comprises 17 Gerrard ordinary shares for 25 King & Shaxson ordinary shares. Shareholders in Gerrard will own around 62.7 percent of the merged entity, which will be called Gerrard Group, and King & Shaxson shareholders 37.3 percent.
Annual cost savings from the merger, which is expected to enhance earnings per share, are estimated to be not less than five million stg, before one-off rationalisation costs.
Brian Williamson, currently executive chairman of Gerrard, will become non-executive chairman.

At the same time, Gerrard announced a pre-tax interim profit for the period to end September of 6.3 million stg, down sharply from 12.1 million stg a year ago. The dividend was unchanged at 8.0 pence per share.
The enlarged group expects to declare a final dividend of not less than 8.0 pence per Gerrard prdinary share for the year to end March 1997.

"The introduction of the gilt repo market, reduced turnover in foreign exchange and increasing margin pressure in derivative markets combined to create a particularly challenging trading environment," the company said.
"Although GNL has built up a significant market share in gilt repo, activity has primarily been with professional counterparties and margins are slim and profitability disappointing."
Shares in GNL fell 21-1/2 pence to 277-1/2p by 0746 GMT, after earlier touching a new 1996 low of 275p. King & Shaxson gained 22-1/2p to 185p, after hitting a 1996 high of 193p.
GNL added that since the end of the half year, it has reviewed the group's cost base and begun to implement a cost cutting plan seeking 3.5 million stg savings in a full year.
The associated rationalisation costs have been included in the period to September 30.
The two companies had their origins in the discount and money markets, but have moved to diversify their sources of income in recent years.
Since an initial investment in 1982, Gerrard has built up leading financial futures and options broker GNI Holdings. In 1987, it bought private client stockbroker Gerrard Vivian Gray.
King & Shaxson has developed a private client stockbroking and fund management busines through the purchase and integration of Greig Middleton and Allied Provincial.
"The integration of Greig Middleton and GVG will reinforce further Greig Middleton's position as a leading full service stockbroker in the UK," said the two companies.
Over the course of next year, the new group will move all settlement office administration for the enlarged stockbroking business to Greig Middleton's settlement office in Glasgow.
"The integration of the stockbroking businesses will also permit the realisation of substantial cost savings."
Consolidation of Gerrard and King & Shaxson's money market business will release at least 25 million stg in capital for investment in the group and future acquisitions.

Following the merger, the money market business will trade as "Gerrard & King" and the stockbroking business as "Greig Middleton". Mark Kemp-Gee will be chairman of the stockbroking business and Norman Andrews chief executive.
